Needs a service account Mixpanel lets import (Admin or Owner on the project).

Each entry is a TextKit event name and the Mixpanel events that count as it, like { event: "purchase_completed", mixpanel_events: ["Purchase Completed", "Web Trial Successful"] }. tools.name: create_automation
tools.title: Create automation
tools.description: Create a triggered text flow (as a draft): when trigger.event is tracked, run steps such as send_sms, wait, wait_for_event, and condition branches. Example: on cart_abandoned, wait 3600s, then if checkout_completed was not received send a reminder. A send_sms step with send_time: "optimal_user_time" and max_wait_seconds (60 to 86400, required) waits for the hour that person usually replies or clicks, 10am their time with no history, inside quiet hours: recommend it for marketing and lifecycle texts, leave it off anything time-sensitive, and it is refused for one-time codes and order or shipping texts. For events that repeat, trigger.cooldown_seconds stops the same person starting it again for that long. Merge fields like {{plan}} fill from the trigger event's properties; `issues` names any no tracked event carries. Leave out `from` and TextKit picks a number approved for `category` (marketing, transactional for alerts, otp for codes) when it sends; `sender` shows the numbers, and `issues` says so when none is approved yet. Pass `from` only to pin a number. Drafts send nothing until activated.

from.description: One of your numbers, to pin the flow to it. Leave it out and TextKit picks a number approved for `category`. A sandbox number makes it a sandbox flow.

category.description: What it sends: marketing, alerts (transactional) or codes (otp). With no `from`, TextKit picks a number approved for this. Falls back to a built-in topic.

topic_id.description: Skip recipients unsubscribed from this topic.

event.description: The tracked event that starts a run

op.description: eq, neq, contains, gt, lt, exists or not_exists

value.description: The value to compare with. Not used by exists or not_exists

filters.description: Up to 5 checks on the event's properties. All must hold

cooldown_seconds.description: Optional. After a run starts for a person, they do not start another for this long (for events that repeat, like a paywall view).

trigger.description: What starts a run: an event, with optional filters

items.description: One of: send_sms {body, from?, send_time?, max_wait_seconds?}; wait {seconds}; wait_for_event {event, timeout_seconds, on_received, on_timeout}; condition {check, on_met, on_not_met}; end. Branches are "continue", "end", or "goto:<id of a later step>".

id.description: Stable handle for goto branches; assigned when omitted.

body.description: send_sms. Merge fields: event properties by name, {{first_name}}, {{name}}, {{phone}}, {{field:<custom>}}.

send_time.description: send_sms: `optimal_user_time` waits for the hour this person usually replies or clicks, inside quiet hours. Default: right_away. Refused for one-time codes and order or shipping texts.

max_wait_seconds.description: send_sms with optimal_user_time, required: the longest this text may wait for that hour

seconds.description: wait: how long, from 60 seconds to 30 days

event.description: wait_for_event: the event to wait for

timeout_seconds.description: wait_for_event: how long to wait, from 60 seconds to 30 days

on_received.description: wait_for_event: where to go when the event arrives: continue, end, or goto:<step id>

on_timeout.description: wait_for_event: where to go when time runs out: continue, end, or goto:<step id>

check.description: {kind: event_received, event} | {kind: property, property, op, value?} | {kind: contact_field, field, op, value?}. op: eq, neq, contains, gt, lt, exists, not_exists.

on_met.description: condition: where to go when the check passes: continue, end, or goto:<step id>

on_not_met.description: condition: where to go when the check fails: continue, end, or goto:<step id>

steps.description: Up to 20 steps, run in order

tools.name: create_segment
tools.title: Create segment
tools.description: Save an audience (a segment, a cohort): it appears in the console under Audience → Segments, and broadcasts can be sent to it. Everyone who can be texted: one rule, status is subscribed. Contacts matching all (or any) of up to 10 rules. Attributes: tags, contact fields, custom fields (field = "field", key = the name), opt-in status, topic, import, created_at. Behaviour: last_message_at, last_reply_at, batch (key = batch id; value included, sent, failed, skipped or replied) and event (key = a tracked event name). Times take an ISO date or a window like 7d. It is evaluated live each time it is used, so a batch or list sent to it reaches whoever matches then.

match.description: all: a contact must match every rule. any: at least one rule

field.description: Attributes: tag, the name and profile fields, source, field (a custom field), import, status (opt-out), topic, list (in a static list), created_at. Behaviour: last_message_at (last text either way), last_reply_at (last text from them), batch (what happened to them in one batch), event (a tracked event; the newest 20,000 events are searched).

key.description: The custom field name (field), topic id (topic), batch id (batch), or event name (event)

op.description: Text fields take is / is_not / contains / not_contains / exists / not_exists; tag takes is / is_not / exists / not_exists; status, topic, import, batch and list take is / is_not; created_at takes before / after; last_message_at, last_reply_at and event take after (at or after the time), before (it happened, and the last time was before it), exists (ever) and not_exists (never). Comparisons ignore case.

value.description: status: subscribed or opted_out. topic: subscribed or unsubscribed. import: an import id. list: a list id (lst_...). batch: included, sent, failed, skipped or replied (sent, then texted the batch's number after it was created). Times (created_at, last_message_at, last_reply_at, event): an ISO date, or a window back from now such as 7d or 24h, read each time the segment is used.

tools.name: send_batch
tools.title: Send batch
tools.description: Send one message to many people (a broadcast or campaign): pick recipients by segment_id, tags, contact_ids, or an explicit recipients list. Opted-out numbers, numbers without marketing consent, and people unsubscribed from topic_id are removed before sending. dry_run: true sends nothing and returns the count, cost, rejected rows and consent. scheduled_at sends at one instant; send_at_local (like 2026-11-10T17:00) sends at that time on each person's own clock.no_opt_in (recipients the send will skip for having no opt-in). Leave out `from` and TextKit picks a number approved for `category` (marketing unless you say otherwise), one per recipient; `sender` shows them, and with none approved it answers 400 and sends nothing. scheduled_at sends later (up to 30 days). shorten_links: true tracks link clicks: suggest it whenever the text has a link. Each recipient can carry external_id (their Mixpanel distinct_id) so the text's events land on their Mixpanel profile. With a live key it texts real people.

from.description: One of your numbers, to pin the batch to it. Leave it out and TextKit picks a number approved for `category` (marketing unless you say otherwise), the same one per recipient. Nothing approved is a 400.

body.description: The message text. Merge tags fill per recipient

With a Mixpanel integration connected, each event about this text lands on that profile in Mixpanel. Without it, the contact with this number that Mixpanel supplied is used.

contact_ids.description: Send to these contacts, by id

segment_id.description: Send to the contacts in this saved segment, evaluated when the batch is created (instead of recipients).

list_id.description: Send to the contacts in this list, as it is when the batch is created (instead of recipients).

topic_id.description: Subscription topic. Recipients unsubscribed from it are removed at validation (`topic_unsubscribed`) and skipped at send time, like opt-outs. Omit to apply opt-outs only.

shorten_links.description: Optional. Rewrite every http(s) link to a tracked short link, per recipient, when each message is sent. Clicks show in GET /batches/{id}/results.

scheduled_at.description: Future ISO timestamp or epoch ms, up to 30 days out.

tools.name: send_message
tools.title: Send message
tools.description: Send one SMS from one of your numbers. Set category "marketing" for promotions (the opt-in check applies) and scheduled_at to send later. Quiet hours apply to every message: outside 8am-9pm (narrower in some states) in the recipient's local time a marketing message is refused and anything else is held until 9am, except one-time codes and replies within 4 hours of their text. In sandbox (test keys), delivery is simulated: +15005550006 delivers, +15005550002 fails, +15005550007 is filtered as spam, +15005550013 delivers after a delay, +15005550016 has no opt-in (see /docs/sandbox).

from.description: One of your numbers, or a sender pool id (pool_...): TextKit picks a pool member, the same one for each recipient every time. Optional when the account has exactly one number for the key's mode.

customer_id.description: Optional. Attribute to one of your customers. Defaults to the customer the from-number is assigned to; a number assigned to another customer is rejected (400).

scheduled_at.description: Optional. Future ISO timestamp (or epoch ms), up to 30 days out. The message is queued and the response is a scheduled_message object instead of a message. A marketing message scheduled into the recipient's quiet hours is refused now (403 quiet_hours) or, with quiet_hours defer, moved to their next 9:00am; any other message is moved.

category.description: Optional. It can make a message stricter (`marketing`), never looser: what a message is comes from the sending number's registration and its wording ([which messages are marketing](/docs/compliance-checks#which-messages-are-marketing)). A message outside its registration's use case is refused with 403 campaign_mismatch.

quiet_hours.description: Optional. What to do with a message in the recipient's quiet hours: `block` refuses it (403 quiet_hours), `defer` holds it until their next 9:00am. Omitted: the account default (a single marketing send is refused; every other message is held). One-time codes are never held.

shorten_links.description: Optional. Rewrite every http(s) link in `body` to a short link with clicks tracked (`links` on the message, `message.link_clicked` events): on <your business>.txtkto.com once your business is verified, txtkto.com before that, or your own link domain when you have an active one (POST /link-domains). The links are checked as you wrote them; texts are counted on the shortened body. Works with scheduled_at.

tags.description: Optional. Your own labels, up to 10 (letters, digits, space _ . : -; up to 32 characters each; lowercased), for example a campaign or a flow. Stored on the message, sent on its webhook events, and reported by GET /v1/deliverability?group_by=tag. Filter with GET /v1/messages?tag=.

consent.description: Optional. How the recipient agreed to your messages. A recurring non-marketing message from a number linked to a registration needs an opt-in on file for that registration; when none is, this records it and the message is sent. Never counts for marketing (use POST /v1/consent with proof). Not with scheduled_at.

collected_at.description: When they agreed: ISO timestamp or epoch ms, not in the future.

page_url.description: Required for web_form: the page the form was on.

media.description: Reserved for MMS; currently returns 400 mms_not_enabled.

status_callback.description: Optional. Also send this message's status events (message.sent, message.delivered, message.failed, message.blocked) to this https URL, signed with your callback secret (POST /v1/webhooks/callback_secret; 400 callback_secret_required until it exists). Logged and retried like a webhook endpoint, under endpoint `status_callback`. Immediate sends only.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Retries are already safe: the same call with the same inputs within 10 minutes is done once and answers with the first result. Pass your own key to dedupe across a longer gap, or a new one to repeat an identical call on purpose.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Retries are already safe: the same call with the same inputs within 10 minutes is done once and answers with the first result. Pass your own key to dedupe across a longer gap, or a new one to repeat an identical call on purpose.
